create.name: Pádraig Ó Tuama
create.bio:
Pádraig Ó Tuama is an Irish poet and theologian whose work keeps returning to belonging, language, conflict and faith. He trained in theology and in mediating conflict within groups, earned a doctorate at the University of Glasgow that brought poetry and theology together, and from 2014 to 2019 led the Corrymeela Community, Ireland's longest-running peace and reconciliation community, whose daily prayer book he compiled. He is now a professor at Yale Divinity School, where he teaches spiritual practice, and a visiting scholar in conflict resolution at Columbia University.

Many people know him as the voice of Poetry Unbound, the On Being podcast in which he reads a single poem slowly and then reflects on it, an approach he brings to retreats and workshops at Omega, Kripalu and elsewhere. In those gatherings he reads poems closely with a group, asks why each one needed to be written, and gives time for participants to write. His books include the memoir In the Shelter, the anthologies 44 Poems on Being with Each Other and Poetry Unbound, and the collections Readings from the Book of Exile, Sorry for Your Troubles, Kitchen Hymns and Love Between Men.

books.title: In the Shelter: Finding a Home in the World
books.author: Pádraig Ó Tuama
books.description: A memoir in short chapters about home, faith and belonging, shaped by an Irish idea that people live in one another's shelter. Ó Tuama draws on his years in reconciliation work, his questions of faith, and the ordinary words we use to greet and hold each other.

books.title: Daily Prayer with the Corrymeela Community
books.author: Pádraig Ó Tuama
books.description: The morning, midday and evening prayers used by the Corrymeela peace community in Northern Ireland, gathered into a book for individuals and groups. The prayers carry the community's long work of bringing divided people together.

books.title: Poetry Unbound: 50 Poems to Open Your World
books.author: Pádraig Ó Tuama
books.description: Fifty poems from around the world, each followed by Ó Tuama's reflection on what the poem notices and what it asks of a reader. The book grew out of his podcast of the same name.

books.title: 44 Poems on Being with Each Other: A Poetry Unbound Collection
books.author: Pádraig Ó Tuama
books.description: A second Poetry Unbound anthology, this time on friendship, family, community and strangers. Each poem comes with a short, warm commentary on how it shows people meeting one another.

books.title: Sorry For Your Troubles
books.author: Pádraig Ó Tuama
books.description: Poems built from ten years of listening to people whose lives were marked by conflict in places such as Northern Ireland and the Middle East. They give voice to loss, memory and the slow work of peace.

books.title: Readings from the Book of Exile
books.author: Pádraig Ó Tuama
books.description: His first poetry collection, which plays with scripture, parable and doubt, written while he was part of the Ikon community in Belfast. The poems question and rework familiar religious language.

books.title: Borders and Belonging: The Book of Ruth: A Story for Our Times
books.author: Pádraig Ó Tuama, Glenn Jordan
books.description: A poet and a theologian read the Book of Ruth together as a story about migration, outsiders and kindness across divides. They link the ancient text to borders and polarised politics today, in Ireland and beyond.

books.title: Kitchen Hymns
books.author: Pádraig Ó Tuama
books.description: A collection of poems that wrestle with God, desire and the body while staying close to ordinary life: animals, trees, food and family.

books.title: Love Between Men
books.author: Pádraig Ó Tuama
books.description: Poems on desire, Irish history and faith. At the centre is a sonnet sequence about attempts by religious groups to change his sexuality, written with candour and an eye towards peace.

books.title: Feed the Beast
books.author: Pádraig Ó Tuama
books.description: A bold collection in which poetry and prayer sit side by side, mixing humour, tenderness and argument with the sacred.

courses.title: Open Your World With Poetry
courses.description: A weekend at Omega's Rhinebeck campus spent reading poems closely, talking about them and writing. Ó Tuama asks why each poem needed to exist and what it reveals about being human, and leaves space for participants to write and share. Beginners and experienced writers are both welcome.
courses.price: Member $335 USD, standard $375 USD (tuition; accommodation extra)

courses.title: Poetry Is (Not) Prayer
courses.description: A weekend at Kripalu in Stockbridge, Massachusetts, also offered by livestream, on how poems and prayers resemble and differ from each other. The group reads and discusses poems, writes, and spends time in quiet reflection.
courses.price: $365 USD per person, plus required accommodation

courses.title: Poetry is (Not) Like a Prayer
courses.description: A six-day writing workshop at the Collegeville Institute in Minnesota comparing prayers and poems through their form, desire and who they address. Daily prompts may lead to poems, prayers, liturgies or blessings. Places are by application, due 13 December 2026.
courses.price: No fee for accepted writers (the Institute covers workshop fees, room and board and most travel within the continental US)

free_resources.title: "How to Be Alone" Poetry Practice
free_resources.description: A short guided writing exercise filmed for Omega in which Ó Tuama invites you to write a poem of advice to yourself.

free_resources.title: Living Your Life in the Company of Poetry
free_resources.description: An hour-long recorded conversation with Omega about how poems can accompany a life, with readings along the way.

free_resources.title: When a Poem Looks Back at You, What Does It See?
free_resources.description: A free audio episode from Omega in which he talks about how a poem can read its reader as much as the other way round.

free_resources.title: Poetry Unbound
free_resources.description: His free podcast from On Being Studios. Each short episode offers one poem, read twice, with a reflection in between.

flags: Fit: he is a poet and theologian rather than a meditation or energy teacher. I kept him because his teaching is openly about prayer, contemplative reading and spirituality (Yale professor in the Practice of Spirituality, former leader of the Corrymeela community, prayer book author); the owner should confirm.

Email is his literary agency's address (Elizabeth Milne at C&W Agency, for Clare Conville), shown as a 'via this email' mailto link on his contact page; the page has no web form of its own. North American speaking goes through Blue Flower Arts' enquiry form.
Possible editorial stature: Poetry Unbound reaches a large audience, but podcast numbers don't count, so I left the tier at local_hero with no override.
His linktree carries affiliate and sponsor links (apps, meal kits); none used.
Love Between Men's blurb mentions 'reparative therapy' and exorcism as subjects of the poems; no health claim, kept.
Kripalu retreat starts 18 Dec 2026; Kripalu is a future hub (README §18.7), so it is linked as an offering only and not in teaches_at.
left_out: 'Healing Spiritual Trauma' (with Thomas Hübl) and a video on a friend's death by suicide: condition-framed titles.
Margaret Atwood interview and Reading Rilke panel: he is interviewer or one of several speakers.
Poetry craft events (Poets House intensive, Arvon masterclass, readings and festivals): literary events, not spiritual teaching, or run by others with no dates read.
What Were You Arguing About Along the Way? (edited by Pat Bennett), Book of Tiny Prayer, Touch the Earth and Between the Bells: contributed or co-authored titles not checked on Amazon in this pass.
Hello: a Spirituality of Welcome (UK edition of In the Shelter) and A Casual Kindness: duplicates or not checked on Amazon.
